implementation_notes: Thread::Queue#close is the built-in pill: after the last push, close makes every waiting pop return nil once the queue is empty, and already-queued items are still handed out first, so the loop is the idiomatic while (item = q.pop) ... end. One close stops all consumers - no per-worker sentinel and no reserved value. After close, push/enq/<< raise ClosedQueueError, which inherits StopIteration, so producers must finish before the queue is closed. SizedQueue offers the same protocol with producer backpressure.
code_sketch:
q = Thread::Queue.new
workers = Array.new(4) { Thread.new { while (item = q.pop); process(item); end } }
# ... q << job ...
q.close                 # drains buffered items, then pop returns nil
workers.each(&:join)
pitfalls: After close, push/<< raises ClosedQueueError (a StopIteration subclass) - close only after the last real push.
deq(true)/pop(true) (non-blocking) raises ThreadError on a closed empty queue instead of returning nil, unlike the default blocking form.
A legitimate nil pushed as a work item is indistinguishable from the closed-queue nil; use a distinct sentinel object when payloads can be nil.
Closing from the consumer side races with live producers; ownership of close belongs to the producer side.
